metadata.case_name: TSANG YUEN NAM v. HUNG YUN METALWARE CO. LTD.

injuries.description: crushing injury to his right knee rupturing both front and back cruciate ligaments
source: As a result of the accident the plaintiff, then 23 and now 27 years old, sustained a crushing injury to his right knee rupturing both front and back cruciate ligaments.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain involving anterior or posterior cruciate ligament of knee

injuries.description: trouble with the donor site in his left knee and was an inpatient for over three weeks
source: He had trouble with the donor site in his left knee and was an inpatient for over three weeks.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg, unspecified

manifestations.description: He suffers residual laxity in the anterior cruciate ligament.
This leaves him with a permanent instability in his right knee.
Muscle wasting in the right thigh was good evidence that his complaints were genuine.

Those complaints included weakness, instability and stiffness in the knee and pain on walking more than modest distances and after prolonged standing and getting up after long sitting and on squatting.
He was in a plaster cast for three weeks.
He was on walking sticks for a month and a half thereafter.
He had trouble with the donor site in his left knee and was an inpatient for over three weeks.
The result of the instability is that he is faced with difficulty in working in the squatting position and he needs to avoid heavy work.

treatments_received: He was in a plaster cast for three weeks.
Arthroscopy in August 1998 revealed the ligamental damage.
Operation to reconstruct the ligaments in June 1999
He was on walking sticks for a month and a half thereafter.
He had trouble with the donor site in his left knee and was an inpatient for over three weeks.
Thirty-eight more sessions of physiotherapy followed.

losses.description: Permanent instability in his right knee with residual laxity in the anterior cruciate ligament, weakness, instability and stiffness, and pain on walking more than modest distances and after prolonged standing and getting up after long sitting and on squatting.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Prior to the accident the plaintiff was a fit young man who played sport. The loss to the recreational side of his life is significant.
The plaintiff is unable to follow his previous skilled employment which involved heavy lifting.
